subject: A Tamil woman in her early thirties, wearing a handwoven Chettinad kandangi cotton sari in muted brick-red and mustard checks, quietly drawing a small traditional pulli kolam with rice flour at the inner threshold; candid everyday concentration, natural posture, no theatrical posing.

setting.place: A Chettinad merchant home courtyard in Karaikudi, Sivaganga district, Tamil Nadu; lime-plastered walls, carved Burmese teak pillars, an open-to-sky mutram, and locally made Athangudi floor tiles.
setting.era: circa 1930, represented with historically plausible domestic details and no modern objects

lighting: Soft, cool pre-sunrise ambient light entering the open courtyard, subtle natural shadow, realistic exposure, no artificial glow.

camera.shot: medium-wide environmental shot showing the woman, kolam, and courtyard architecture

style: Photorealistic historical documentary photography, restrained and intimate, natural skin texture and fabric weave, lived-in domestic atmosphere, culturally grounded rather than staged or postcard-like.
avoid: generic pan-Indian or North Indian visual motifs
Thanjavur temple gopurams or palace architecture
generic silk sari; use the specified Chettinad kandangi cotton textile
Bharatanatyam costume, dance pose, or theatrical jewellery
oversized bindi, excessive gold jewellery, or glamour styling
tourist-poster composition, oversaturated colours, artificial HDR
modern appliances, plastic objects, electric fittings, cars, phones, or synthetic fabrics
fantasy details, inaccurate architecture, text, logos, watermark, extra fingers, malformed hands

motion.subject_motion: The woman steadily completes a few small curves of the rice-flour kolam; the loose end of her sari moves almost imperceptibly in the early morning breeze.
motion.environment_motion: A faint movement of leaves visible above the open courtyard; otherwise the courtyard remains still.
motion.camera_move: Very slow, subtle push-in from the same eye-level observational angle; no cuts or sudden movement.
